feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong CV with clear positioning for senior digital communications roles and credible progression within one organization. It reads professionally and shows solid scope, but impact would be stronger with more quantified outcomes, and there is some redundancy across skills sections.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level brand: the headline, summary, and role progression consistently support a digital strategy/communications leadership profile.  
- Good credibility: long tenure at NACo with promotions, major platform work, and relevant tools/platforms creates a believable, well-aligned narrative.  
- Writing is polished and generally concise, with strong action verbs and clear coverage of web, content, analytics, and multimedia leadership.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable results beyond scope metrics: include outcomes such as traffic growth, engagement lifts, email performance, cost savings, production efficiency, or adoption improvements.  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap significantly; consolidate to improve structure and save space.  
- Fix minor style/grammar consistency issues: add “of” in “more than 12 years of experience”; keep serial commas consistent (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs. later lists without the final comma); “cross-channel communications” and “multi-channel communication” are slightly inconsistent in style. No obvious misspellings or major typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be sharper with a more distinctive value proposition, tighter phrasing, and fewer generic claims already covered elsewhere.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” and lead with seniority plus sector relevance.
- Replace broad lists (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”) with a tighter summary of outcomes: cross-channel strategy, platform modernization, and operational leadership.
- Add public-sector/advocacy context to better match the NACo experience and strengthen positioning.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience advancing web, content, email, social, and multimedia programs for mission-driven and advocacy-focused organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, Drupal and platform modernization, and the workflows, governance, and analytics systems that enable high-performing digital operations. Skilled at stakeholder coordination and translating complex policy or technical issues into clear, accessible communications.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows and systems” repeat heavily in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Stakeholder coordination” also appears in Soft Skills; keep it here only if framed as a strategic strength.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant mix of strategic, technical, and communications capabilities, but several items are broad or repetitive with the header and Topline Skills. Tightening wording and emphasizing higher-value leadership themes will make this section sharper.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and tighten wording: “Multi-channel communications,” “Cross-functional stakeholder coordination,” “Web platform and CMS administration.”
- Prioritize more senior, differentiating strengths first: digital transformation, editorial systems/governance, analytics, platform architecture.
- Consider a more targeted version: Digital strategy & transformation • Editorial systems & governance • Web platform & CMS administration • Multi-channel communications • Data analytics & reporting • Workflow & systems architecture • Cross-functional stakeholder coordination • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia & live event production
- Keep style consistent: pluralize “communications” and “systems” where appropriate.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Overlaps heavily with the header (“cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” “stakeholder coordination,” “advocacy messaging”).
- Also duplicates Topline Skills; if both remain, make Core Competencies broader and reserve tools/details for Topline Skills.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo role below and the Recent Projects section. Tighten it around consultant-level impact, transformation outcomes, and what is new since returning in 2024.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancements, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery initiatives.”
- Replace generic verbs (“consult,” “build and refine,” “deliver”) with outcome-oriented phrasing: “Redesigned workflows,” “launched campaign microsites,” “improved governance,” “led AI search initiative.”
- Consolidate into 3–4 bullets and add measurable outcomes where possible: number of microsites/toolkits launched, workflow time saved, publishing teams supported, traffic/member usage, search accuracy or engagement improvements.
- Emphasize what is distinct from prior full-time role: consulting scope, campaign builds, AI search, and cross-channel governance—not general website/email/social oversight.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital systems, workflows and analytics” overlaps with Director of Digital Media; specify new consulting deliverables.
- Microsite and AI search language duplicates Recent Projects; either quantify here or keep project detail there, not both.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, budget, and multi-channel content operations across web, email, social, and video.”
- Combine and streamline channel bullets; focus on scale + result: “Oversaw email and social programs reaching tens of thousands of county officials, strengthening advocacy distribution and audience engagement.”
- Make outcomes more explicit where possible: add % improvements, cost savings, production volume, turnaround time, engagement growth, or reporting adoption for the Drupal migration, analytics stack, and video studio.
- Tighten wording: replace “along with” and long tool lists with impact-led phrasing, e.g., “Built an enterprise analytics stack (GA4, BigQuery, BI dashboards) to improve leadership reporting and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this version more strategic and outcome-focused.
- Video expansion may overlap with older NACo roles and footer projects; emphasize building the studio and organizational capacity, not routine production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry reads generic and overlaps with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role. Make it more execution-focused and quantify scope so it shows promotion-ready impact without repeating higher-level leadership claims.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a tighter scope statement: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, supporting advocacy campaigns and organization-wide editorial execution.”
- Replace “helping” language with direct action: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Add measurable outcomes if available: newsletter open/click rates, video cadence/views, audience growth, turnaround time, or number of cross-functional teams supported.
- Combine the last two bullets into one sharper line: “Built cross-team editorial planning and standardized publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations” overlaps with the Director of Digital Media entry; keep this role focused on management/execution, not enterprise leadership.
- Weekly advocacy video work also appears in the 2015–2018 role and footer project list; emphasize expansion/regularization here.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies and reads generic rather than differentiated. Tighten it to emphasize leadership scope and public-sector relevance without repeating adjacent sections.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, higher-signal wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “audience-focused content planning” for “content operations” or “content strategy” to sound more senior and align with recent leadership roles.
- Keep terminology consistent with recent experience: use “governance,” “operations,” and “enterprise” since those recur credibly in 2022–present roles.
- If space allows, add one differentiator not covered elsewhere, e.g. “organizational change leadership” or “publisher enablement.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” overlaps with both Core Competencies and multiple NACo role bullets.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. For a topline skills area, emphasize higher-value capabilities tied to recent Drupal modernization and AI/search work, not every platform.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Put the most relevant/recent strengths first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations/automation.
- Remove lower-priority platforms unless required by the role; WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages are better kept in “Technical + IT.”
- If space allows, sharpen impact language: “Enterprise Drupal platforms” or “Large-scale CMS modernization” instead of just “Drupal” / “CMS modernization.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; avoid repeating the same platform inventory in both places.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies, so keep wording distinct or consolidate.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for the recent NACo leadership work, but it reads as a generic tool list. It would be stronger if framed around business value and differentiated from the separate “Technical + IT” analytics list.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize outcomes, e.g. **Analytics, Reporting & Optimization**
- Replace the pure list with grouped, impact-oriented phrasing:
- **Analytics stack:** GA4, Microsoft Clarity, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI
- **Measurement:** KPI framework design, dashboarding, leadership reporting
- **Optimization:** SEO analysis, user behavior insights, performance monitoring
- If space allows, add one qualifier tied to recent scope: “enterprise reporting” or “decision-support dashboards”
- Keep wording parallel with other Topline Skills sections; avoid overloading with too many tools

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Technical + IT → Data, Analytics & Optimization**; keep this section strategic/outcome-focused and leave the detailed tool inventory there
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating that exact phrasing

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

- Video production and editing

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the Core Competencies line and multiple NACo roles. Make it more senior, operational, and outcomes-oriented rather than listing basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe for leadership scope: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ/multi-camera production systems • Multimedia program development”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with a more strategic phrase like “Broadcast-quality video production” or “End-to-end multimedia production” to better match Director-level experience.
- Replace “Livestreaming” with “Livestream and hybrid event delivery” to sound more complete and audience-facing.
- If space allows, add scale/context in adjacent experience bullets instead of here (e.g., studio built, recurring advocacy programming, event support).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same wording.
- “Studio operations” and “hybrid/virtual event production” are already evidenced in recent NACo roles, so this skills line should stay concise and differentiated.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior digital leader, this item should signal level of use and emphasize the most current, high-impact platform first.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by strength/relevance: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites)** • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- If space allows, add light qualifiers instead of just names: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; modular microsites)** • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- Consider tightening the title to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing.
- If no qualifiers are added, consider dropping **GitHub Pages** unless it reflects meaningful recent use; it reads lighter than the rest.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; keep one list detailed and the other abbreviated.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent NACo roles, so avoid repeating the same platform names elsewhere without added context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical range, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Make it sharper by emphasizing implementation depth and tools that support recent, higher-value work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Technical Implementation: HTML/CSS/JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop versioned/basic labels (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless the CV is targeting hands-on developer roles; they add little at senior-leadership level.
- Consider replacing “jQuery” with “Front-end scripting” or moving it to the end if still relevant; it can date the profile unless the target roles explicitly require it.
- If accurate, add scope/outcome context elsewhere, e.g., “front-end implementation for Drupal microsites,” “serverless scripting for web workflows,” or “deployment automation for site updates.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- GTM may also overlap conceptually with analytics tooling; keep it here only if used for implementation, not reporting.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow leadership. Since the CV already emphasizes automation and governance, this item should be tighter and grouped to signal systems thinking, not just familiarity.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe by function, e.g.: “Workflow automation & collaboration: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier; project and editorial operations: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp; team coordination: Slack, Microsoft Teams.”
- Put the strongest, most relevant tools first: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana.
- If accurate, add scope in parentheses to increase credibility: “Airtable (workflow databases), Power Automate/Zapier (cross-platform automation), Jira/Asana (project tracking).”
- Consider shortening to 6–7 tools max; Basecamp, Trello, Slack, and Teams are lower-signal unless central to your recent work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Slack/Teams overlap with general workplace tools and may dilute stronger technical platforms.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as generic software inventory rather than evidence of current email/engagement capability. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this item should stay concise and emphasize enterprise-grade systems over basic tools.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/seniority: “Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp”
- If space allows, sharpen the label to: “Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms”
- Consider adding functional context instead of just names: “Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (journey orchestration) • Higher Logic (member communications) • Mailchimp”
- Only keep Mailchimp if you used it meaningfully in recent work; otherwise remove it to keep the list more senior and current.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with repeated “email/newsletters” references in Work Experience; avoid adding descriptive claims here that duplicate those bullets.
- “Engagement” may partially overlap with “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies, so keep this item tool-focused.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more concrete by emphasizing “firsts,” team-building, and specific outputs or scale.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground advancement and foundational impact: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Tighten the second sentence around 2–3 concrete contributions: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and helped expand day-to-day digital production capacity.”
- If possible, add metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, email/social volume supported, or size/timeline of the website refresh.
- Replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with a stronger leadership phrase if accurate: “mentored” or “supervised” a digital media associate.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on launching/building the capability rather than expanding it.
- “Strengthening workflows” repeats themes from later roles; position this as the initial foundation.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Emphasize the distinctive innovation/research scope and tighten the media language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground scope and initiative: “Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting county-focused programs and policy initiatives.”
- Make the podcast launch the lead accomplishment: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- Tighten the supporting media point: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications and policy storytelling.”
- If possible, add one concrete outcome: number of episodes launched, audience/downloads, stakeholder groups served, or types of research/projects coordinated.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later Digital Media Manager / Producer and Associate Communications Director entries; keep this item lighter on broad multimedia claims.
- Avoid repeating “oversaw planning, scripting, and production” if similar production language appears elsewhere; “launched” is the differentiator here.
